title: Add rollback dry-run emulator and Helm constraint enforcer
author: Priya N. Rao
description: Motivation: Upgrades for private deployments must have a low blast radius and the ability to verify a rollback without touching production state. This PR implements two complementary safety mechanisms: a rollback dry-run emulator (emulator) that simulates an in-place rollback sequence against an ephemeral clone of cluster state, and a Helm constraint enforcer that gates Helm value sets and chart versions during upgrade/rollback orchestration. Summary of changes: 1) installer/upgrade: add 'upgrade-dryrun-emulator' binary and operator API hooks. The emulator performs an automated sequence: snapshot export, ephemeral namespace restore, execute rollback steps (helm release rollback, CRD reduction/restore, DB migration reversal using migration runner in read-only mode), and post-run verification that checks service account bindings, KV cache compatibility, and storage layout. 2) operator: add UpgradePlan validation webhook that runs Helm constraint checks and consults chart version pinlist to block unsupported downgrades. 3) terraform: add plan-lock hook that fails concurrent apply attempts for clusters with an active UpgradePlan. 4) helm: add values schema and enforced constraints (persistence.enabled must be true for replicas > 1, image.tag pinning, pdb minimum available thresholds). 5) docs/tests: add detailed dry-run playbook and new e2e test which performs a synthetic rollback against a cloned Postgres dataset. Design notes: - The emulator is intentionally non-destructive: it uses snapshot/restore to a namespaced clone so no production DB, manifests, or PVs are modified. - Constraint enforcer exposes a 'strict' and 'permissive' mode; default is 'strict' for release channels tagged 'enterprise'. - Terraform plan-lock integrates with the existing state backend and writes an UpgradeLock object to the installer operator; this avoids split-brain upgrades. - All changes are configurable via operator Helm values under 'upgradeSafety'. How to test locally: - make dev-upgrade-emulator: runs integration-dryrun using testdata snapshots. - rictl upgrade dry-run --cluster <test-cluster> --plan <plan-id> will run the emulator and upload artifacts to the specified workspace. Backwards compatibility: the operator will reject UpgradePlans that request downgrades unless 'allowDowngrade' is explicitly set and an approved bypass token is provided. Rollout plan: merged to main, feature flagged off by default. Gradual enable for staging clusters, then opt-in for customers. Related: ENG-9321 (upgrade safety), ENG-9410 (helm gating), SUP-5482 (customer incident followup).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can the emulator be run without a full DB snapshot? Author: yes; emulator supports logical pg_dump-based dry-run for smaller testcases
Ava Chen: Helm constraint enforcer should surface which specific constraint failed with a link to remediation steps. Action: added detailed error payloads and remediation links
Samir Patel: add metric for 'dryrun_success_rate' for monitoring. Action: added Prometheus metric and Grafana dashboard panel
QA: observed intermittent failure in e2e when underlying storage class reclaim policy is Delete; added additional cleanup and wait logic
ci_logs_summary: Most checks green. Integration dry-run initially flaked due to timing; fixed by adding wait for PV binding. Terraform plan step now emits a warning when plan-lock is present; CI runs in warn mode to allow merge after manual review.
merge_info: Merged by: Ava Chen; method: squash; commit: 'squash: add rollback dry-run emulator and helm constraint enforcer'
release_notes: Added a non-destructive rollback dry-run emulator and a Helm constraint enforcer to reduce upgrade/rollback risk for private deployments. New operator UpgradePlan validation and terraform plan-lock guard help prevent concurrent or unsupported upgrades. Includes CLI support (rictl upgrade dry-run) and e2e test coverage.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests added for webhook logic and emulator orchestration; integration-dryrun verifies end-to-end rollback simulation against an ephemeral Postgres clone; manual staging run performed on staging cluster 'stg-us-west-2' and results validated by SRE; promoted to canary after 48h with no regressions.
notes_for_operators: Feature disabled by default. To enable: set charts.private-installer.upgradeSafety.enabled=true and configure chartVersionPinlist and planLock.backend. If enabling in production, schedule a maintenance window and run rictl upgrade dry-run for each target cluster to collect artifacts before performing real upgrades.
changelog_entry: Implement rollback dry-run emulator and Helm constraint enforcement to reduce upgrade blast radius; add terraform plan-lock integration; add rictl dry-run command and docs.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: emulator performs non-destructive operations; however, added operator webhooks and terraform hooks change upgrade gating behavior and must be carefully configured. Default keeps safety checks off for self-hosted until explicitly turned on.
post_merge_tasks: create linear task to add UI support in Console for dry-run artifacts (ENG-9570)
